summary: Standing 100-ft LS-40 Aermotor tower in the Francis Marion NF; Forest Service used it to 1989, SC Forestry Commission staffed it to 1993, and it now sits in a camping area.

facts.design: LS-40 100-foot Aermotor tower with a 7 x 7 ft metal cab and hip roof.

access.note: Inside the Honey Hill Recreation Area, a primitive camping area on the Francis Marion National Forest. The Forest Service says the tower is no longer in use.

visit.trail_note: From Charleston, take US 17 north to McClellanville, turn left onto SC 45 and drive eight miles to the camp. A short camp loop circles the tower.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Francis Marion National Forest)

events.note: U.S. Forest Service use of the tower ended in 1989, per the NHLR.
The South Carolina Forestry Commission staffed the tower until October 1993.
Registered December 1, 1998; nominated by Glen Stapleton, District Ranger.

evidence.supports: 100-foot LS-40 Aermotor tower with 7 x 7 ft metal cab and hip roof; used by the Forest Service until 1989.
evidence.quote: The LS-40 100’ Aermotor tower with 7’ x 7’ metal cab and hip roof was used by the U.S. Forest Service until 1989.

evidence.supports: Built in the 1930s; oldest remaining tower in one place on the forest; one of several fixed-point detection lookouts.
evidence.quote: Honey Hill Lookout, constructed in the 1930s, is the oldest remaining tower in one location on the Francis Marion National Forest and was one of several lookout stations used in the comprehensive fixed-point fire detection of the earlier years of the Forest Service.
The South Carolina Forestry Commission staffed it until October 1993.

evidence.supports: Within a national forest picnic area; maintained on standby status.
evidence.quote: Located within a Francis Marion National Forest Picnic area, it is maintained on standby status.

evidence.supports: Register places the lookout in Charleston County.
Primitive camping area with a short camp loop encircling the tower; tower no longer in use; vault toilet, picnic tables, grills.
evidence.quote: This primitive camping area is located between McClellanville and Honey Hill. A short camp loop swings through an upland pine/oak forest and encircles a fire lookout tower. The fire lookout tower is no longer in use. Vault toilet, picnic tables, grills.

evidence.supports: Driving directions from Charleston to the camp.
evidence.quote: From Charleston, take US Highway 17 north to McClellanville. At the intersection of SC Highway 45 (the yellow caution light) turn left, and drive eight miles to the camp.

evidence.supports: Eastern lookouts site places the tower in Berkeley County.

sources.title: Honey Hill Recreation Area
sources.publisher: U.S. Forest Service, Francis Marion and Sumter National Forests

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR places the tower in Charleston County; the eastern lookouts site lists Berkeley County. The record has no county field, and the story reports both.

notes_for_editor: NHLR gives only the 1930s for construction, so no built event is recorded. Staffing status none rests on the Forest Service statement that the tower is no longer in use and on NHLR standby status; the as_of date is the research date, and the staffing end (1993) is the last documented date. The county conflict is unresolved. No climbing information was found in the sources read, so visit.climbable is omitted. Hillmap and the OpenStreetMap node were checked but add no history. No new photos.
